chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from a number of our companions from Ali ibn Asbat from Husayn ibn Harithah from Muyassar ibn Abd al-Aziz said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do not do business with one who has a chronic ailment/disability, for they are the most unjust of people.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on trading with people who have chronic illnesses or disabilities according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) cautions against commercial dealings with those suffering from a chronic ailment or disability ('awha), characterizing them as 'the most unjust' (azlam) in their transactions. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of 'adl (justice) in trade, suggesting that physical or mental vulnerability may predispose individuals to exploitation or to acting unfairly due to their condition, thereby warranting caution for the merchant to ensure equitable exchange.
